Local to the Sunshine Coast · Based in Palmwoods

Sunshine Coast School Incursions

Looking for Sunshine Coast school incursions with a difference? Rhythm Culture is a local team, so we bring West African drums, music and dance straight to your school. What’s more, we visit schools right across the coast, from Noosa to Caloundra and out to the hinterland.
Get a Quick QuoteSee all school programs
For primary and high schools. No travel fees on the Sunshine Coast.
Local teamWe live and work on the Sunshine Coast, in Palmwoods.
No travel feesWe come to you, so there’s nothing extra to pay for travel.
Free drum hireEvery student plays a West African Djembe at no extra cost.
1,500+ groupsWe’ve worked with over 1,500 schools, kindergartens and OSHC services.
Why choose a local team

Why Sunshine Coast schools book Rhythm Culture

Because we’re based on the coast, planning an incursion with us is simple. Getting to your school is easy, so we can fit in around your term calendar.Also, every session is tailored to your students. So whether you need a small group workshop or a whole-school event, we’ll shape the program around your year levels and timetable.As a result, Sunshine Coast schools book us for many different occasions:
  • Harmony Week and cultural days.
  • Music and performing arts programs.
  • Whole-school events and special celebrations.
  • Student wellbeing and team-building days.
  • End-of-term celebrations and school retreats.
Choose a program

Our school incursion programs

There are three programs to choose from. Each one suits primary and high school students, and no experience is needed.
Most popular

Drum Sing Dance

Students drum, sing and dance in one lively session. Then they bring it all together as one big ensemble.About Drum Sing Dance →
Music

African drumming

Every student plays a djembe, so the whole class learns rhythms, call-and-response and ensemble playing.About the drumming workshop →
Dance & performing arts

African dance

Students learn energetic West African moves. Live drumming can also be added for a bigger experience.About the dance workshop →

In addition, we visit local kindergartens and OSHC services, such as Peregian Beach Community Kindergarten, Mudjimba C&K and Coolum OSHC. So see our kindergarten incursions and vacation care incursions too.Want to see one in action? Then read about our visits to Sunshine Beach High School, Glasshouse Christian College and St Teresa’s Catholic College.

Booking a Sunshine Coast school incursion

  1. 1. Request a quoteFirst, send us your school, preferred dates and year levels.
  2. 2. Plan togetherThen we suggest the best program and timings for your students.
  3. 3. We drive to youOn the day, our local team brings every drum and sets up in your space.
  4. 4. Play as oneFinally, the session ends with everyone playing together as one ensemble.

Sunshine Coast school incursions FAQs

Do you charge travel fees for Sunshine Coast schools?No. We’re based in Palmwoods, so there are no travel fees anywhere on the Sunshine Coast. In fact, we don’t charge travel fees anywhere in Australia.
Which areas of the Sunshine Coast do you visit?All of it. We visit schools all over the coast, from Noosa and Coolum to Kawana and Caloundra, as well as hinterland towns like Maleny, Nambour and Glass House Mountains.
Can you run sessions for the whole school in one day?Yes. We can run several sessions for different year levels, or bring everyone together for one big session. So just tell us your timetable, and we’ll plan around it.
Do your incursions link to the curriculum?Yes. Our programs support The Arts (Music and Dance) as well as cross-curriculum learning about cultures. For example, see how our school incursions link to the curriculum.
How do we book a Sunshine Coast school incursion?Simply fill in our quick quote form, or call 0434 585 992. Then we’ll come back to you with options and pricing for your school.

Drum Sing Dance Program

Rhythm Culture’s Drum Sing Dance program is packed full of interactive fun while being educational and multicultural. Along the way, children drum, sing and dance their way through the amazingly diverse cultures of West Africa.
Get a Quick QuoteSee the five workshops
We visit kindergartens, schools and OSHC services across the Sunshine Coast, Brisbane and Australia-wide.
Free drum hireEvery student plays a West African Djembe at no extra cost.
No travel feesOur artists visit services Australia-wide, so you never pay travel fees.
Trained in AfricaAll our artists have also studied and trained in West Africa.
Package discountsMultiple incursion bookings also receive fantastic savings.

Why choose our Drum Sing Dance program?

With so many different countries, instruments and dances to choose from, we guarantee you and your children fun and entertainment. At the same time, children learn about the amazingly diverse cultures that live in West Africa.For this reason, our Drum Sing Dance program is the best way for your children to have an exciting, interactive and multicultural experience. What’s more, there are five different workshops to choose from, so we have your programs and incursions covered for the entire year.In addition, booking multiple incursions gives you fantastic savings.
Program benefits

Drum Sing Dance program benefits

All of these benefits are part of our Drum Sing Dance program. Even better, children experience them in a fun, playful and engaging way.
MusicalChildren drum, sing and also play lots of instruments.
PhysicalDancing also builds coordination and spatial awareness.
InteractiveEvery child has an instrument, so everyone plays.
EducationalChildren also practise counting, language, listening and following directions.
SocialTeamwork and communication then build connection and community.
CulturalStories and play bring African culture to life, so learning feels natural.
CreativeThinking, playing and movement all come together.
What happens?

What happens in a Drum Sing Dance program workshop?

Each workshop runs for 30 to 50 minutes. During that time, the children go on a journey through story, song and movement.
  • First, every child plays an African drum and unique African percussion.
  • There is also body percussion, plus call-and-response music patterns.
  • Then we share lots of singing, dancing and laughing.
  • Children also learn real African dance moves.
  • We ask lots of questions, so everyone stays involved.
  • Finally, children discover how African instruments are made, and what they are made from.
Check availability
Choose your workshop

Five Drum Sing Dance program workshops

There are five workshops to choose from, so you can book something new each term. As a result, children explore a different West African country or dance style every time.
Guinea

Groovers in Guinea

  • First, play the djembe (hand drum).
  • Then dance the BIG JUMP.
  • Next, speak Sousou, an African language.
  • It’s super fun and active!
Mali

Imagination in Mali

  • Journey to Bamako, Mali in West Africa.
  • Then hear the ancient sounds of the balafon.
  • Dance with your friends, dance with everyone!
  • Finally, play the tama, the drum that talks!
Ghana

Get Down in Ghana

  • First, sing the beautiful melodies of Ghana.
  • Then play drum solos.
  • Next, dance the moves of Kpanlogo.
  • Finally, clap your hands and get down in Ghana!
Traditional

West African Dance Rumble

  • What’s that over there? There’s a rumble in the distance!
  • Then learn traditional dance moves.
  • Next, dance an African story.
  • Finally, shake your shoulders and rumble those feet!
Modern

West African Pop Party

  • First, hear the modern sounds of West Africa.
  • Then dance the latest modern moves.
  • Next, create your own African-style dance moves.
  • It’s fun, active and the beats are pumping!
Not sure which workshop to pick? Just tell us your group’s ages and interests, and then we’ll recommend the best fit.
Who it’s for

Who is the Drum Sing Dance program for?

The program suits kindergartens, early learning centres, primary schools, OSHC and vacation care services. Because every child has an instrument, nobody waits on the sidelines. Also, no experience is needed, so it works well for mixed ages and abilities.

For primary & secondary schools

African Drumming & Dance School Incursions

Our school incursions bring the energy of West Africa to your students. They are hands-on, fast-paced and educational, so everyone is involved. In addition, every student plays their own West African drum.
Get a Quick QuoteCompare workshops
We run school incursions across the Sunshine Coast, Brisbane, Melbourne, Sydney, Adelaide and Perth.
Free drum hireEvery student plays a West African Djembe at no extra cost.
No travel feesOur artists visit schools Australia-wide at no extra travel cost.
Trained in AfricaAll our artists have studied and trained in West Africa.
West African drumsAuthentic instruments that sound great.

Bring the energy of African drumming to your school

Rhythm Culture’s Drum Sing Dance school incursions are packed with exciting rhythmic activities, so your students will be on the edge of their seats. Through traditional West African rhythms, students connect through music, movement and sound. As a result, everyone gets involved in a lively, hands-on experience.For example, students explore coordination, connection and musical dynamics. They also discover tempo and rhythm through the incredible sound of the djembe. Above all, our workshops are fast-paced, engaging, educational and great fun!

Experience the culture behind the rhythms

What makes our school incursions special is the cultural knowledge our artists bring. All our facilitators have studied in West Africa, so they share personal stories, musical knowledge and first-hand experience of Africa’s diverse traditions.As a result, students don’t just learn to play a drum or follow a dance step. Instead, they experience the culture, history and traditions behind the music.
Sunshine Coast school?We’re a local team based in Palmwoods, with no travel fees anywhere on the coast.
See our Sunshine Coast school incursions

Choose from three school incursions

Every workshop is tailored to your students’ year level and abilities. Not sure which one suits you best? In that case, we’re happy to talk it through.
Most popular

Drum Sing Dance

Drumming, singing and dance combined. First, students rotate through all three. Then they bring their skills together in one energetic ensemble.Great for: Harmony Day, rewards days, end-of-year celebrations and whole-school events.
Music

African Drumming Workshop

Traditional West African rhythms on authentic djembes, as well as rhythm games, call-and-response and ensemble playing.Great for: Music classes, Under 8s Day and cultural studies.
Dance & performing arts

African Dance Workshop

Rhythmic footwork, body percussion and dynamic West African movement. Live drumming can also be added.Great for: Primary groups, as well as secondary dance students building choreography for assessment.
African drumming workshops

Every student plays a West African drum

Students are introduced to traditional West African rhythms and, at the same time, the excitement of playing authentic drums as a group. Through rhythm games, call and response and ensemble activities, they build listening skills, coordination and teamwork.No previous drumming experience is needed, so students of every ability can join in. In addition, all drums are West African drums, which means a beautiful sound and an authentic experience.

Just like in Africa, we use our voice

Rhythms are spoken, sung and sounded out, so voice and body come together. Call-and-response activities also help students listen, respond and communicate rhythmically, even without a musical background. After all, everyone has a voice, and every voice becomes part of the rhythm!Encourage diversity: for example, schools hosting Harmony Day or Under 8s Day often include drumming to celebrate cultures, peers and friendship.
African dance workshops

Energetic, expressive West African dance

Our African dance incursions combine rhythmic footwork, body percussion, coordination and dynamic movement. Students therefore explore the relationship between music and dance while building confidence. Dance workshops can also include live African drumming.

Primary school students

Fun, upbeat choreography inspires creativity and is a great energy release. It also builds a sense of community within the cohort.

High school students

Students learn a West African dance they can then combine with contemporary pieces for assessment. It’s also a fun way to release study pressure. We offer it as a one-off introduction or as a series of sessions.
West African dance differs dramatically from many styles taught in Australia. For this reason, students learn about traditional and modern dance in Africa, signature moves and their cultural significance. They also discover the stamina, endurance and focus the style demands.
Drum Sing Dance

Drumming, singing & dance in one action-packed session

Students learn funky drumming and dance breaks based on traditional West African rhythms. First, they alternate between drums, dance and traditional songs. Then everyone comes together as one ensemble. Because it’s fast-paced and adaptable, it suits large groups and every age level.

Traditional rhythms from Guinea, Mali & Ghana

Rather than simply learning a collection of beats, students discover the foundations of traditional rhythms. They also hear the stories and cultural significance behind them, shared by artists who learned them first-hand.Book Drum Sing Dance
For teachers

How it started

Our story

Rhythm Culture started with a shared passion. Co-founders Bec and Nathaniel Combs both fell in love with West African drum and dance in Melbourne, learning from inspiring teachers in a close-knit music community.Before long, that passion took them to the source. Nathaniel travelled to Conakry, Guinea in 2004 to play with leading ensembles, and Bec later studied dance there too. Every trip deepened their respect for the rhythms, stories and people behind the music.In 2012, they brought it all to the Sunshine Coast and founded Rhythm Culture. Their goal was simple: to share the joy of West African rhythm with their new community.Today, that small start has grown into incursions, workshops and performances right across Australia. In fact, Drum Sing Dance is now one of the most popular kids’ incursions on the coast. Meanwhile, our Tuesday night classes in Palmwoods have become a weekly celebration of live music and community.
Our approach

How we share West African music

Everything we teach is based on traditional West African rhythms. So whether it’s a kindy session or a corporate workshop, our approach stays the same.

Traditional rhythms

We keep every rhythm, ensemble and dance as close to its original structure as possible.

Story and song

We also include story and song in every lesson, so people understand what each rhythm means and why it’s played.

Our teachers keep studying and training in West African culture. As a result, what we share stays authentic.
